question: Should OpenClaw adopt the shared notificationWake.reactions policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical opt-in reaction-turn contract, or choose a narrower channel/per-message design instead?
rationale: Current main has passive reaction system events and a heartbeat primitive, but the missing behavior adds public wake/config semantics across multiple bundled channel plugins.

options.title: Adopt Shared Wake Policy
options.body: Use a queue/wake/off notification wake policy as the canonical default-safe contract, then repair or land the best candidate with docs and channel tests.

options.title: Choose Narrower Contract
options.body: Start with Discord, Telegram, or per-message awaitReaction semantics, accepting that cross-channel parity will need a later product pass.

options.title: Defer Reaction Wakes
options.body: Keep reactions as passive system events for now and pause or close implementation candidates until maintainers want this config surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Wake Policy
recommendation.body: Use a queue/wake/off notification wake policy as the canonical default-safe contract, then repair or land the best candidate with docs and channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the open shared-policy candidate and is the best current routing target for choosing that product/API surface.
